author: skogul valkyrie (sonnet-5)
title: Warm-referral velocity test, isolated from cold-Upwork channel
hypothesis: Olrun's short-term-1 folds Upwork-cold-post and warm-referral into one bucket with one probability (40-60%), but their base rates diverge sharply -- Upwork AI/ML agency reply rate is 7.21% (over-fished), while warm-referral hiring literature puts referred-candidate conversion at 4-10x cold. Splitting the channel isolates which half is actually driving the number, and warm-referral is testable in days, not weeks.
method: Send a 1-paragraph personalized note plus the 60-second gesture-tracking demo link to 10 people already in the operator's existing network per day for 5 days (50 total). Ask each for either (a) a paid intro call, or (b) a forward to one person who needs AI-eng help.
cost: near-zero -- time only, no tooling or ad spend
timebox: 5 days to send, 7 days total to collect replies
kill_criterion: fewer than 3 substantive replies (call booked or qualified forward) out of 50 by day 7 -> deprioritize warm-referral as a distinct channel and fold remaining effort back into general Upwork/job-hunt activity
expected_revenue_relevance: directly informs whether short-term-1's 40-60% estimate is realistic or is being propped up almost entirely by the referral half -- a cheap test that de-risks the highest-ranked recommendation in Olrun's own list

author: skogul valkyrie (sonnet-5)
title: Micro-price test on one polished gesture-tracking module, before the full Product Hunt launch bet
hypothesis: Olrun treats the spatial-app recommendation as a single all-or-nothing 30-day PH-launch event (10-25% chance of 'meaningful revenue'). Solo-dev revenue data shows meaningful revenue realistically takes 12-18 months of sustained work, not one launch -- so testing raw willingness-to-pay on ONE small module first, at near-zero cost, tells us whether the bigger studio bet (long-term-1) is worth making before spending launch-week effort on the full app.
method: Put a $9-19 Gumroad paywall on one already-polished gesture-tracking module or demo (not the whole app). Drive traffic via zero-cost channels only: relevant subreddits, HN 'Show HN', and 1-2 niche Discord/spatial-computing communities. Target 100 targeted visits over 7 days. Measure visit-to-purchase conversion.
cost: near-zero -- Gumroad listing is free, distribution channels are free/organic
kill_criterion: zero purchases at 100 visits -> willingness-to-pay signal is absent at this price/packaging; revisit price point or packaging before any full-scale PH/studio push
expected_revenue_relevance: cheap leading indicator for both short-term-3 (spatial app revenue) and long-term-1 (studio viability) -- de-risks the bigger, slower bets with a fast, nearly-free proxy test

author: skogul valkyrie (sonnet-5)
title: Manual reply-rate A/B across two verticals, before paying the 14-21 day Instantly warmup cost
hypothesis: 2026 cold-email benchmarks show reply rate varies 3x by vertical (recruitment/staffing 5-8%, legal up to 10%, versus generic B2B SaaS 2-4%). Olrun's short-term-4 assumes a single target (spatial/XR startups) and a tooled Instantly campaign requiring a 14-21 day warmup before it's safe to send volume. Testing vertical choice manually and cheaply, before paying that warmup cost, determines whether the Instantly investment is worth making at all.
method: Hand-send 20 personalized cold emails/DMs total with no automation tooling: 10 to recruitment/staffing-adjacent AI-eng brokers (highest-reply-rate vertical per 2026 benchmarks), 10 to spatial/XR startups directly (Olrun's implicit target). Track replies per group over 7 days.
cost: zero -- manual sends from an already-reputable personal/existing inbox, no new domain or tooling
kill_criterion: if the spatial/XR group underperforms the recruitment/staffing group by 2x or more, redirect the eventual Instantly campaign's ICP before paying the 14-21 day warmup cost; if both groups reply below 2%, deprioritize cold outreach further behind Olrun's already-last ranking
expected_revenue_relevance: prevents sinking the 14-21 day warmup cost (which already eats half of any 30-day short-term window) into the wrong ICP -- highest-leverage cheap test for the lowest-ranked but still-planned channel

author: nidhoggr-adversary valkyrie (sonnet-5)
title: Sell what is already built: a flat-fee setup service for the $0 near-frontier compute mesh (Ollama + LiteLLM + LangGraph)
adversarial_case_vs_olrun_top3: This is the only proposed lane that monetizes an artifact ALREADY BUILT AND PROVEN rather than requiring new production or a competitive bid. Olrun's short-term-1 (Upwork) requires winning against a crowded field from a 0-rated profile (see this vote's own AGAINST row); this requires no bidding -- inbound-only via one organic post. It also requires zero build time: this same voting session independently verified the mesh is real (11 local Ollama models, a documented OLLAMA_HOST fix already written up in contracts/dollar_zero_mesh_activation.v0_1.md) and separately verified it is NOT fully wired (LiteLLM proxy non-responsive, a memory-mismatched model). That gap between 'proven concept' and 'not fully wired' is exactly the kind of hands-on troubleshooting a buyer would pay a flat fee to skip.
hypothesis: A single organic post in r/LocalLLaMA or r/selfhosted ('I run near-frontier AI for $0/month across 11 local models plus a router -- DM me to set yours up, flat fee') generates inbound leads at a materially lower cost-per-lead than cold Upwork bidding, because it targets an audience that already wants this specific thing rather than a generic buyer who must be convinced.
method: Write and post once to 1-2 relevant subreddits/forums. Offer a flat $150-300 setup fee (video call + written runbook, using this forge's own contracts/dollar_zero_mesh_activation.v0_1.md and cost_tier_routing.v0_1.md as the reusable deliverable template). No new build required -- the offer IS the existing infra, packaged.
cost: near-zero -- one post, reused documentation, ~1-2h per client call once a lead converts
timebox: 7 days to post and collect DMs, 14 days to close first paid setup
kill_criterion: zero substantive DMs within 7 days of posting -> the pain point is not real or not monetizable at this price point; do not repeat with a second post before revising price or audience
expected_revenue_relevance: directly tests whether 'sell what's already built' beats 'compete for what's already crowded' (Olrun's short-term-1) -- a cheap, fast falsifier for an entire class of income lane Olrun's ranking did not consider at all

author: nidhoggr-adversary valkyrie (sonnet-5)
title: Skip the agency: pitch ONE corporate marketing team directly with the live handpiano.com demo, capture full activation budget instead of a subcontract slice
adversarial_case_vs_olrun_top3: This forge's own Ship Readiness doc (M1) already validates the exhibit/kiosk/experiential-marketing thesis at $3-8K/module against a $40-80K full install, but routes it through 20 agencies for a subcontract slice, explicitly reasoning 'an agency buys one module, a brand requires you to sell the whole install' as a reason to AVOID direct brand sales. That reasoning treats deal size as pure risk without weighting it against outreach volume: this experiment requires ONE well-targeted pitch instead of 20 agency contacts, using the exact same already-live asset (handpiano.com, HTTP 200, verified). Lower volume, same marginal cost per attempt, larger deal size if it lands -- a genuinely different risk/reward point Olrun's ranking excluded rather than evaluated.
hypothesis: At least one marketing team at a brand already known to run experiential/interactive activations will take a discovery call from a cold but highly specific pitch (named live demo, named use case, named budget range) at a meaningfully higher rate than the 20-agency M1 lane's implied per-contact conversion, because the pitch is concrete and demoable rather than a generic subcontractor introduction.
method: Identify 3-5 brands with recent (last 12 months) experiential/interactive marketing activations (trade show, pop-up, kiosk). Send one direct, specific email to the marketing team or agency-of-record contact per brand, linking handpiano.com live and naming a concrete activation concept. No new build -- the asset already exists.
cost: near-zero -- research + 3-5 emails, a few hours total
timebox: 14 days to send and collect first replies
kill_criterion: zero discovery calls from 5 direct-brand contacts within 14 days -> the direct-to-brand channel is not viable at cold-outreach volume; fall back fully to Olrun's M1 agency-subcontract lane rather than repeating direct attempts
expected_revenue_relevance: tests whether a smaller number of higher-value direct pitches beats the agency-subcontract volume play Olrun's ranking defaulted to without testing the alternative -- cheap enough to run in parallel with M1, not instead of it

author: nidhoggr-adversary valkyrie (sonnet-5)
title: Live-code the swarm build (Twitch/YouTube), converting the 133-generation story from a resume liability into an audience asset
adversarial_case_vs_olrun_top3: This vote's own AGAINST row on short-term-2 (job/recruiter outreach) argues the 18-19 month gap reads as a hiring-manager red flag. Build-in-public is the one lane that converts the exact same fact into content instead of a liability: iteration-in-full-view is not a gap to a streaming audience, it is the show. It is also the only proposed lane with ZERO opportunity cost against the operator's own building time -- unlike Upwork or job-hunt hours, which compete directly with build time, streaming the build IS the build, with a camera on. It also directly produces the reference-customer/case-study asset that this vote's own row on long-term-3 (HFO methodology consultancy) flags as currently missing and structurally necessary before that lane can work at all.
hypothesis: Streaming actual swarm-build sessions (multi-agent orchestration, the $0 mesh, receipt/chain discipline) to a niche technical audience (r/LocalLLaMA-adjacent, AI-agent-builder Twitter/Discord communities) will, at zero marginal cost beyond turning on OBS during work already happening, produce measurable audience growth and at least one inbound (sponsor, consulting lead, or Patreon-style support) within 60 days -- functioning as a free byproduct exactly the way this forge's own Ship Readiness doc treats Gumroad/GitHub-marketplace listings, a logic it never extended to live content.
method: Stream or record 3-5 sessions of actual in-progress work (not staged content) on Twitch or YouTube, cross-posted to 1-2 relevant communities. No new work created -- capture of work already happening. Track viewer count, follows, and any inbound DMs/comments over 60 days.
cost: near-zero -- OBS/recording software (free tier), a few minutes setup per session, zero additional work-hours beyond what is already being spent building
timebox: 60 days, 3-5 sessions minimum to judge signal
kill_criterion: fewer than 20 total sustained followers/subscribers AND zero inbound messages after 5 sessions -> the audience-building thesis has no early traction at this niche; do not continue investing session-prep time beyond the zero-marginal-cost 'just record what is already happening' version
expected_revenue_relevance: de-risks long-term-3 (HFO methodology consultancy) by generating the missing case-study/reference asset as a free byproduct of work already underway, while also testing a distribution channel Olrun's ranking did not include in either the short-term or long-term list
